newsitem.title: NIGERIA: U.S. will help Nigeria fight drugs war.
newsitem.headline: U.S. will help Nigeria fight drugs war.

text.p: A United States anti-drug team on Wednesday said they will help Nigeria fight traffickers who use the West African nation as a major transit centre for narcotics.

"We had extensive discussions and reached understanding on areas where we can cooperate to fight the drugs war," Jonathan Winer, leader of the American team told reporters at a briefing in the capital Abuja after a three-day visit.
"We hope that the Nigerian efforts will continue towards achieving practical results in the war against drug traffickers and those who commit financial crimes."
In May, Nigeria rejected a U.S. report that said it was not doing enough to beat hard drugs trafficking.
Nigeria, has been "decertified" by the United States twice since 1994, a measure that blocks economic aid and which Washington takes when dissatisfied with a country's effort in the drug war.
On the "decertification" of Nigeria, Winer said: "This was not our brief, but to explore areas of possible cooperation between both countries on drugs and financial crimes war."
Nigeria does not produce heroin or cocaine but has a reputation as a transit point and many Nigerian couriers are serving prison terms abroad.
The military government last year introduced tribunals to try drug couriers.
The U.S. team had discussions with Mohammed Adamu, special adviser to the military government on drugs and financial crimes and head of relevant government agencies.
Relations between the two countries are strained by U.S. criticism of Nigeria's ruling generals for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy.
